content: Disodium phosphate, also known as disodium hydrogen phosphate (Na2HPO4), is a sodium salt derived from phosphoric acid. It appears as a white powder that is highly hygroscopic, meaning it readily absorbs moisture from the air, and it is highly soluble in water. Due to these properties, it is commonly used in commercial applications as an anti-caking agent in powdered products to prevent clumping. This compound is also referred to by other names, including disodium hydrogen orthophosphate, sodium hydrogen phosphate, or sodium phosphate dibasic. It is available commercially in both hydrated and anhydrous forms, depending on the specific application. Other Uses: Disodium phosphate is utilized in food products such as cream of wheat to reduce cooking time, enhancing convenience for consumers. In industrial applications, it is often used in combination with trisodium phosphate in steam boiler systems. In this context, it serves to provide a reserve of free phosphates, which helps to inhibit the formation of calcium scale deposits, thereby improving the efficiency and longevity of the boiler system.
